bibl.title: Djedhor Son of Usirwer in the Valley of the Kings.
bibl.seg: Steve Vinson, Eugene Cruz-Uribe & Jacqueline Jay, Djedhor Son of Usirwer in the Valley of the Kings.

Robert K. Ritner (ed.), Essays for the Library of Seshat. Studies Presented to Janet H. Johnson on the Occasion of Her 70th Birthday = Studies in Ancient Oriental Civilization. 70 (Chicago, 2017) pp. 381-398, figg.
bibl.note: In the Ptolemaic or early Roman period, an ordinary Egyptian priest (an ἰṱ nṯr, "god's father") named Djedhor son of Usirwer son of Imhotep left at least one Demotic graffito in eight tombs in the valley, and might also be the author of four hieratic graffiti. The Demotic graffiti now become a new body of evidence for understanding the phenomenon of visitation of the royal tombs of the Valley of the Kings.
